key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO3 post-perovskite conducts 44–55% more lattice heat than bridgmanite under matched lower-mantle conditions.
engineering_relevance: This computational geoscience study—not solar-cell research—provides thermal-conductivity references for modeling lower-mantle heat transport and core–mantle boundary heat flow.
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine phase-boundary calculations with a model geotherm and aggregate conductivity bounds.
evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, otherwise identical transport calculations using MACE versus DFT forces differ in conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
watch_item: The reported aggregate bounds describe an Fe-free mineral mixture and should not be treated as direct predictions for compositionally complex mantle material.
paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
